description: Composite figure of four panels combining a beamline schematic (a), azimuth-resolved diffraction intensity maps (b), Rietveld-refined integrated patterns (c) and a single-peak fitting example (d), all from in-situ synchrotron HEXRD of a low-density medium-Mn steel. (a) draws fixed-energy photons (60 keV) through a slit system onto the specimen, with a beam stop and a detector annotated with the Debye-Scherrer ring, scattering vector Q, azimuth angle η and the axes TD, ND, LD; a red inset shows dog-bone specimens cut along TD and RD with banded δ-ferrite and α+γ regions. (b) stacks three maps of azimuth angle (0–360°, y-axis) versus 2θ (5–12°, x-axis) for non-deformed, ~30% strained (RD) and ~30% strained (TD), colour-coded to intensity (0–10 ×10⁴ counts), with reflections labelled γ111, α110, γ200, α200, γ220, α211, γ311, γ222 and α220. (c) plots integrated intensity (×10⁴ counts) versus 2θ for the same three conditions, with experimental open circles and calculated solid lines from Rietveld refinement; an inset expands 9–12°. (d) shows the non-deformed RD profile integrated over azimuth −5° to 5° with FCC (green) and BCC (blue) single-peak fits. Together the panels document diffraction-intensity redistribution and austenite→α transformation after 30% tensile strain, differently for RD and TD orientations.

subfigures.description: Schematic of the in-situ synchrotron high-energy X-ray diffraction setup: fixed-energy photons (60 keV) pass a slit system, hit the specimen, and are recorded by a detector marked with the incident beam stop and a Debye-Scherrer ring; labelled axes TD, ND, LD, scattering vector Q, azimuth angle η and diffraction angle 2θ_hkl. A red inset sketches dog-bone tensile specimens oriented along TD and RD containing δ-ferrite and α+γ bands.

Three stacked 2D intensity maps of azimuth angle (0–360°, y-axis) versus 2θ (5–12°, x-axis) labelled non-deformed, ~30% strained (RD) and ~30% strained (TD); a colour bar at right gives intensity from 0 to 10 ×10⁴ counts. Vertical reflection bands are annotated γ111, α110, γ200, α200, γ220, α211, γ311, γ222, α220.

Integrated intensity (×10⁴ counts) versus 2θ (5–12°) curves/point sets for non-deformed, 30% strained-RD and 30% strained-TD, each shown as experimental open circles plus calculated lines; legend distinguishes non-deformed (Cal.) black, non-deformed (Exp.), 30% strained-RD (Cal.) red, 30% strained-RD (Exp.) red circles, 30% strained-TD (Cal.) blue and 30% strained-TD (Exp.) blue circles. An inset expands the weak 9–12° reflections (γ220, α211, γ311, γ222, α220).

Integrated diffraction profile of the non-deformed RD sample over azimuth −5° to 5°, plotted as intensity (×10⁴ counts) versus 2θ (5–12°): experimental intensity-RD as open red circles with FCC (green) and BCC (blue) single-peak fit lines; inset expands 10–12° showing α211, γ311, γ222, α220 and γ220 peak fits.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a schematic, not a photograph: it shows fixed-energy 60 keV photons entering through a slit system, striking the specimen, a beam stop, and a detector plate carrying the Debye-Scherrer ring, with the labels TD, ND, LD, scattering vector Q, azimuth angle η and 2θ_hkl.
The red inset of panel (a) shows two dog-bone tensile specimens with their gauge sections containing banded δ-ferrite and α+γ regions, drawn for the TD and RD loading orientations.

Panel (b) contains three stacked intensity maps sharing the axes azimuth angle 0–360° (ticks 0, 60, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360) and 2θ = 5–12°, labelled non-deformed, ~30% strained (RD) and ~30% strained (TD), with a colour bar from 0 to 10×10⁴ counts.
The reflections labelled in panels (b), (c) and (d) are γ111, α110, γ200, α200, γ220, α211, γ311, γ222 and α220 — five FCC peaks and four BCC peaks.

The legend of panel (c) distinguishes six entries: non-deformed (Cal.) black line, non-deformed (Exp.) open circles, 30% strained-RD (Cal.) red, 30% strained-RD (Exp.) red open circles, 30% strained-TD (Cal.) blue and 30% strained-TD (Exp.) blue open circles.
The legend of panel (d) reads Exp. intensity-RD (open red circles), FCC intensity-RD (Cal.) (green line) and BCC intensity-RD (Cal.) (blue line), and the panel is annotated 'non-deformed'.

In (c) and (d) the α110 peak at the lowest 2θ (about 5.5–5.8°) is the strongest feature, while the γ-family peaks are markedly weaker; the inset in (c) shows the weak γ220, α211, γ311, γ222 and α220 reflections between 9 and 12°.
The caption states that (b) plots diffraction intensity versus azimuth angle and 2-Theta for a non-deformed sample and a sample deformed to 30% applied strain.

The caption states that in (c) both experimental data (Exp.) and results calculated (Cal.) with the Rietveld refinement method are plotted, and that in (d) the profile integrated over azimuth −5° to 5° is fitted with FCC and BCC peaks (green and blue solid lines) using the single peak fitting method.

The citing text states the HEXRD beamline was operated at ~60 keV (~0.20738 Å) with a 0.5 × 0.5 mm² beam size, a Kammrath & Weiss tensile rig at ~1×10⁻³ s⁻¹ initial strain rate, and specimens of 12 mm gauge length, 2 mm width and 1.2 mm thickness.

The citing text states that two sample orientations, denoted RD and TD, were tested with the tests repeated at least three times each, and that 2D patterns were collected with a Varex XRD 4343CT detector every 1 s, calibrated with a standard CeO2 sample.

The citing text states that five crystallographic reflections of the FCC phase ({111}, {200}, {220}, {311}, {222}) and four of the BCC phase ({110}, {200}, {211}, {220}) were identified, matching the peak labels visible in the panels.

The citing text states that the Debye-Scherrer ring was divided into 36 sectors of 10° and the sector along the tensile direction (azimuth −5° to 5°) was selected for lattice-strain analysis, which is what panel (d) illustrates.

The citing text states that the austenite volume fraction was analysed by Rietveld refinement with the MAUD software, and that the calculated profiles (solid lines) match the experimental data (open dots).
